name: Waste collection and sanitation services

problems.words: Customers complain we missed their pickup and we cannot prove we came
quick_ideas: Ask drivers to take one photo at each stop, so there is proof of service
Keep a daily list of stops done and missed, so complaints can be checked against it.

workzap_build.text: Route sheets on phone per truck with stops by area or customer reference, marked done with time and photo, plus a proof-of-service summary for customers.

problems.ask_first: How many trucks run each day?
problems.free_stops: Route sheet design and summary format are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count missed pickup complaints against that day's completed stops for one week, so you see which routes trigger the most disputes.
Give one dispatcher the job of marking every route sheet returned before closing time, so proof of visited stops is kept together.

problems.words: Routes are in the driver's head, so if he is absent nobody knows the route
quick_ideas: Write each route down as an ordered list of stops, so anyone can run it
Have a stand-in ride along once, so cover is ready.

workzap_build.text: booking_scheduling — Written routes on phone with a crew assignment board and stand-in planning.

problems.ask_first: Are most of your routes kept in drivers' heads, or only a few?
problems.free_stops: Route set-up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk one full route with the regular driver and note landmark turns and stop order, so the route can be covered when he is absent.
Keep each route's written stop order in one notebook kept with dispatch, so cover drivers can collect it before leaving.

problems.words: Fuel cost per route is a guess
quick_ideas: Record fuel filled and disposal trips per truck for one week, so you have real figures
Divide by route, so you see which routes cost most; talk to your accountant on how to read it.

workzap_build.text: A cost per route and contract view from fuel, tipping fees, crew and maintenance entered by the owner.

problems.ask_first: Is fuel guessed mostly for collection routes, or for disposal trips?
problems.free_stops: Cost allocation is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write each truck's start and end fuel gauge against the route every day this week, so costly routes are easier to spot.
Make one person note fuel and route together at return time, so cost tracking happens daily without chasing drivers later.

problems.words: Skips sit at sites past the hire period and we do not bill it
quick_ideas: List every skip out with its site reference and hire end date, so overdue ones are visible
Check the list weekly, so extra days are billed.

workzap_build.text: workflow_automation — A skip and bin register with placement date, hire end and overdue alerts for billing.

problems.ask_first: Are the overdue skips mostly at building sites, or at other places?
problems.free_stops: Register and alert design are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare skips currently out on sites with the hire notebook this week, so unbilled extra days are found before they pile up.
Give one clerk the job of reviewing all open skip hires every Friday, so overdue time gets noticed in time to bill.

problems.words: Households in societies pay late or not at all
quick_ideas: Keep one unpaid list by society, so follow-up is shared
Send reminders a few days before the due date, with residents' permission, so payment is front of mind.

workzap_build.text: customer_messaging — A subscriber billing and collection tracker with reminders and online payment links where available.

problems.ask_first: Do the late payers sit in a few societies, or across many?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and wording are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count unpaid households by society at week end in one notebook, so you see where late payment is concentrated.
Give one collector the same follow up hour on the same day each week, so unpaid society accounts are chased routinely.

problems.words: Collectors take cash door to door and deposits are delayed
quick_ideas: Set a fixed deposit day and time for every collector, so late deposits stand out
Match collections to deposits weekly, so gaps are found early.

workzap_build.text: A collector deposit log with variance flags by collector role.

problems.ask_first: Are deposits late by a day, or by several days?
problems.free_stops: Matching rules are in the solution document; pi records the control gap, not names.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each collector's cash noted received with cash handed in on the same day, so deposit delays are easy to spot.
Set one daily cash handover time with one receiving person and one notebook, so collections stop sitting overnight unofficially.

problems.words: Trucks break down and a whole area is missed for days
quick_ideas: Note each truck's last service date, so overdue ones are seen
Agree a backup truck or hire arrangement, so a breakdown does not stop an area.

workzap_build.text: Vehicle maintenance reminders by date and a breakdown log showing areas affected.

problems.ask_first: Do breakdowns come mostly with old trucks, or after heavy loads?
problems.free_stops: Reminder schedule is in the solution document; pi gives no vehicle safety advice.

extra_ideas.text: Note every missed area beside the truck that failed this month, so you see which vehicle causes the most disruption.
Give one staff member the job of checking each truck's condition every return, so small faults get written down before areas are missed.

problems.words: Complaints come via society WhatsApp groups and blow up before we see them
quick_ideas: Give each society one official complaint number, so complaints reach you directly
Reply to every complaint the same day, so it does not grow in the group.

workzap_build.text: Complaint intake from WhatsApp into tickets with response timers and a closure photo.

problems.ask_first: Do complaints concern mostly missed pickups, or staff behaviour?
problems.free_stops: Ticket flow is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count complaints by society and by time received for one week, so you see where messages escalate before your team notices.
Make one person responsible for checking complaint groups at fixed times daily, so issues are seen before they grow publicly.

problems.words: Society management asks for monthly service reports and we make them by hand
quick_ideas: Agree which few figures each society actually wants, so reports are short
Collect them daily from route sheets, so month end is not a scramble.

workzap_build.text: A monthly service report generator for societies and commercial clients built from route records and photos.

problems.ask_first: Do societies want service reports weekly, or monthly?
problems.free_stops: Report format is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Keep a simple daily count of pickups, misses and complaints by society, so month end reporting pulls from one running note.
Give one office person one notebook for all society service figures each day, so monthly reports stop being rebuilt from scattered papers.

problems.words: Helpers do not turn up, especially after Eid
quick_ideas: Keep a simple daily attendance list per crew, so gaps are known by morning
Line up stand-ins before Eid, so routes still run.

workzap_build.text: A crew attendance and daily assignment board with stand-in planning for peak and holiday periods.

problems.ask_first: Do helpers miss work mostly after Eid, or all year?
problems.free_stops: Board set-up is in the solution document; pi records no workers' personal details.

extra_ideas.text: Mark expected and actual helpers per crew for one week in one notebook, so post Eid absence patterns are clear.
Make one supervisor responsible for confirming each crew the evening before, so morning departures are less disrupted.

problems.words: Recyclables go to the kabari and we never know if we got a fair weight
quick_ideas: Weigh recyclables yourself before each sale, so you have your own figure
Record weight and rate at every sale, so patterns show.

workzap_build.text: A recyclables sales log with weights and rates recorded at each sale and a monthly summary.

problems.ask_first: Is the kabari your only buyer, or do you sell to several?
problems.free_stops: Log design is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each recyclables load by material and estimated sack count before it leaves, so sale weights can be compared later.
Give one person the job of writing every recyclables sale in one ledger, so disputes over fair weight are easier to challenge.

never_say: Anything on handling, classifying or disposing of hazardous, medical, chemical or industrial waste, protective equipment or confined-space entry.
Anything that helps with illegal dumping, burning, mixing waste to avoid fees or bypassing permits.
Any request for customer addresses and phone numbers or workers' names, IDs and personal circumstances.
Any help with bribery around municipal contracts or permits.
Anything other than emergency services when a worker is in a sewer or septic tank in difficulty, or gas, fire or injury is described.

sample_reply.person: Society wale har hafte shikayat karte hain ke gaari nahi aayi, aur hamare paas koi saboot nahi hota. Kya karein?
sample_reply.pi:
Bilkul, is ka hal mumkin hai, aur is ke liye bade kharch ki zaroorat nahi.
Pehle, driver har stop pe ek photo le, taake service ka saboot ho.
Doosra, rozana done aur missed stops ki list rakhein, taake har shikayat us se mila sakein.
Workzap is se aage ye kar sakta hai: har truck ka route phone pe, har stop waqt aur photo ke saath mark ho, aur har society ke liye proof-of-service report khud ban jaye.
